inputs.share_count_basis: POST 3-for-1 split effective 2026-10-01 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin, subsequent events): 96,204,351 shares issued less treasury 1,085,235 (361,745 at 2026-06-30 x 3) = 95,119,116. No dilutive securities exist (tanshin: 潜在株式が存在しない). Held flat: SBC is zero and buybacks are the mechanism that keeps the count flat. NOTE the Metrics CSV shares (31.7m) and EPS history (e.g. FY2026 349.58) are PRE-split; the Yahoo price and 52-week range are post-split, so this file uses the post-split count. Pre-split equivalent price = 5,280.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 yuho / tanshin cash-flow statement: no share-based payment line; only a small directors' BIP share trust whose shares sit in treasury. SBC-zero market -- house and street bases coincide.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q1 FY2027 (2026-06-30) consolidated B/S: short-term loans 18,129 + current LTD 9,527 + current bonds 5,000 + bonds 30,000 + LTD 25,431 = 88,087 (CP nil); cash and deposits 14,741. J-GAAP filer: no lease liabilities on the balance sheet, operating leases are expensed inside operating income. Pension nets to an asset (5,815 asset vs 1,023 liability at 2026-03-31) and is left out.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY. Cost of equity 8.5% = 10y JGB ~1.7% + 1.1 beta x 6.0% Japan ERP (levered cyclical). After-tax cost of debt ~1.0% (FY2026 interest 1,279 on ~87bn debt = 1.5% pre-tax, 31% statutory). Market-value weights ~65/35 (market cap 167bn vs debt 88bn) give 5.9%; the house uses 7.0% to allow for BoJ normalisation lifting the JPY risk-free rate over the 10-year horizon and for refinancing of a debt stack that is 2.4x EBITDA. Cyclicality itself is priced in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate, and the same WACC is used in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: None required: J-GAAP, operating leases expensed in EBITDA, no lease liabilities on the balance sheet. Net debt is borrowings and bonds only.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; non-controlling interests (2,642 at 2026-06-30) deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI share of profit is small (<1bn/yr).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: non-US cyclical industrial -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). First valuation of this ticker. Flows are built from operating income + D&A, so interest income (129), dividend income (1,089) and equity-method income (265) are all outside the flows; last_fcf strips the 1,218 of interest+dividends from the 1,878 reported FCF (OCF 34,539 - capex 32,661) and the matching asset -- the investment-securities portfolio -- goes into the equity bridge at after-tax value. Buyback_cash 5,018 is actual FY2026 financing outflow; the count is flat and funded. FY0 is the year ended 2026-03-31. FY2027 guidance (maintained 2026-08-04): sales 234.5bn, OP 15.0bn, NI 10.0bn, capex 27.1bn, D&A 24.3bn, DPS 40 post-split (120 pre-split floor). FY2026-28 medium-term plan (repo FY2027-FY2029): sales 255.5bn, OP 27.0bn by FY2029, 100-110bn cumulative investment, ROE 9%+, total payout 50%+. The prior plan's FY2026 OP target of 21.4bn was missed by 36% (actual 13.6bn); base haircuts the new plan, bull hits it. The 70% Sumisho Cement acquisition reported in the Analysis JSON (close targeted 2026-10-01) does not appear in any filing in this folder and is NOT modelled -- a thin-margin distributor consolidation would raise revenue more than FCF, and its purchase price would add to net debt; revisit when the H1 FY2027 tanshin (Nov 2026) discloses it. Cash taxes: statutory 31.0%; FY2026 effective 29.1%; FY2026 cash paid 2,162 was low on timing and residual loss carryforwards (now ~1bn), so the cash rate ramps 27 -> 31% over three years. Working capital: manufacturer with receivables + inventory > payables, capture set at -10% of the revenue change.

equity_bridge.note: FY2026 yuho securities note: listed cross-shareholdings fair value 32,016 on cost 3,289 (unrealised gain 28,727) at 2026-03-31; total investment securities 42,948 at 2026-06-30 (down 782 on sales). Listed portion ~31.2bn less 31% tax on ~27.9bn of gain = ~22.6bn, plus ~11.4bn of unlisted/affiliate stock at book = ~34.0bn. Matches the stripped dividend and equity-method income (adaptations rule d). Company is actively selling policy stock (6,379 proceeds FY2026, 5,849 FY2025).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (FY2023 -> FY2026), cross-checked against FY2027 guidance of +4.8% and the plan's +4.4%/yr to FY2029; equity CAGR is depressed by buybacks (10.4bn FY2022, 5.2bn FY2025, 5.0bn FY2026) and the FY2023 loss
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - 0 SBC - interest income (pre-FY2020 interest income not in the pivot; immaterial at <0.1bn). 3-year FCF and EPS CAGRs are undefined: FY2023 was a loss year (net income -5,719, owner FCF -44,136) when coal spiked before cement price increases caught up. 5-year owner FCF fell from 12,518 (FY2021) to 660 (FY2026) because capex rose from 20.2bn to 32.7bn (ESC plant, kiln work) while EBITDA only recovered to 37.2bn vs 35.4bn; this is the capex supercycle, not SBC. Ten-year revenue is flat (234.2bn FY2016 -> 223.7bn FY2026) -- domestic cement demand fell from 37.3Mt (FY2023) to 30.0Mt forecast FY2027 and price increases have only just offset it.

base.narrative: FY2027 on guidance (sales +4.8%, EBITDA 16.8% = OP 15.0bn + D&A 24.3bn). Plan haircut: revenue reaches ~248bn by FY2029 (plan 255.5bn) and EBITDA 18% (OP ~20bn vs plan 27bn), then growth fades to 1% as cement volume decline (-2 to -3%/yr) is only offset by price and ESC. Capex runs at 13% through the plan's ESC build-out and settles at 10.5%, just above D&A. Cash tax ramps to the 31% statutory rate. Terminal capped at 15x FCF for a cyclical, secular-decline core.

bull.narrative: The FY2026-28 plan is delivered: sales 255.5bn and OP 27bn in FY2029 (EBITDA ~20.4% with D&A 10.5%). Electrostatic chucks ride the AI-capex cycle at mid-teens segment margins, the new ESC building fills, cement pricing holds above energy costs, and the oligopoly keeps margin as volume shrinks. Growth stays at 1.5-2% beyond the plan as high-functionality materials become ~15% of sales.

bear.narrative: A milder replay of FY2023: coal above the $140/t plan assumption and a yen weaker than 155 squeeze cement before the next price round lands, while the semiconductor-capex cycle turns in FY2028-29 and the new ESC capacity is under-utilised. Sales stall near 230bn, EBITDA margin drops to 14.5% and only recovers to 15.5% (FY2025 level), capex still has to be spent on the plan's commitments, and the optoelectronics unit stays loss-making.

scenario_narratives.base: Management's FY2027 guidance is taken at face value and the FY2026-28 plan is discounted by roughly the same margin by which the previous plan was missed: OP reaches ~20bn (not 27bn) in FY2029 on ~248bn of sales. Domestic cement demand keeps falling toward 30Mt and the oligopoly's price increases roughly offset it, so group growth fades to 1% once the ESC capacity ramp is absorbed. Capex stays above D&A through FY2030 and then normalises; the business converts ~3-5% of revenue into owner FCF, which is why the equity is worth far less than its EBITDA multiple suggests.
scenario_narratives.bull: The plan is hit: electrostatic chucks (guided +73% profit in FY2027) keep compounding on AI-driven fab capex, the high-functionality segment grows from 9% to ~15% of sales at mid-teens margins, cement pricing stays ahead of energy costs, and policy-stock sales keep funding buybacks. EBITDA margin reaches 20%+ and holds; terminal growth 1.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Energy costs and yen weakness outrun cement pricing again (the FY2023 pattern) while the semiconductor cycle turns against the just-completed ESC building. Revenue stalls, EBITDA margin falls to the mid-14s before recovering only to FY2025's 15.5%, and the plan's committed capex still goes out the door; FCF is marginal for several years and the debt stack (2.4x EBITDA, with 2.4bn of CP/short-term loans rolling) limits buybacks.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the core business swung to an operating loss as recently as FY2023 on a single input (coal), leverage is 2.4x EBITDA with meaningful short-term refinancing, and the bear path does not require anything exotic. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it requires the plan to be delivered after the previous plan was missed by 36%, and depends on one product line (ESC) in a cyclical end-market. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the consolidated operating flows (operating income + D&A, after cash tax, capex and working capital) at a JPY cost of capital, cap the terminal at 15x FCF because the core is a capex-heavy cement business in secular volume decline, then bridge to equity with borrowings/bonds, NCI and the after-tax cross-shareholding portfolio. SBC is nil, so house and street coincide. The split (3-for-1, 2026-10-01) is reflected in the share count; the price and 52-week range are post-split.
key_risks_to_valuation: Coal/oil and JPY/USD: each $1/t of coal or JPY1/USD moves operating income by ~0.6-1.3bn; a repeat of FY2023 wipes out a year of FCF
Plan execution: FY2029 OP target of 27bn vs base 20bn; the prior plan was missed by 36%
Semiconductor capex cycle for electrostatic chucks, which carry the whole profit-growth story
Capex overrun: 100-110bn planned over three years against ~24bn of D&A; the model assumes capex normalises to 10.5% of sales from FY2032
Sumisho Cement (70%) acquisition is not modelled: purchase price and consolidation effect unknown from filings
Cross-shareholding bridge (34bn after tax) depends on equity-market values and on management continuing to sell policy stock
Pre-split EPS and share figures in the Metrics CSV will produce a wrong P/E if divided into the post-split price
